title: Eylema — Composable Agentic AI Platform in Rust
description: Explore Eylema: a Rust foundation and local task console for a platform of cooperative agentic loops, compatible models and human-controlled learning.
headline: From intent
to action.
By design.
intro: A platform in development for cooperative agentic loops. Connect roles, replace compatible models and turn permitted experience into reviewed training data.
status: Rust task core and local browser console implemented. Integrated model, workflow and learning capabilities still need acceptance.

architecture_intro: Eylema owns the platform contracts and lifecycle. Perception, planning, decision and optional prediction roles cooperate around Rust authority and observed results.
technology_alt: EylemA architecture v0.5: human-governed stable contracts connect perception, planning, decision, optional prediction, XState workflow and Rust execution. Observed results feed back; permitted data follows a separate training, evaluation and safe model-activation loop.
technology_caption: Architecture v0.5 proposal. The operating loop produces observed results; a separate permitted-data loop uses external Unsloth training and independent evaluation before safe activation. The implemented Rust task foundation is distinct from integrated model/XState acceptance.

steps.name: Compose
steps.title: Define a reusable loop.
steps.text: Connect roles through versioned observation and action contracts. Set goals, permissions, termination conditions and finite budgets. Placement and document-evidence applications should share these platform contracts.

steps.name: Assign
steps.title: Replace models, safely.
steps.text: MiniCPM, Qwen and local policies are candidate participants, not the platform identity. Accept exact artifacts, operators and hardware profiles; compare a replacement on held-out tasks and activate it between steps. In-flight work retains its assignment.

steps.name: Inspect
steps.title: Separate proposals from facts.
steps.text: The proposed local XState workflow coordinates bounded work; Rust independently checks authority, current state and budgets. Link each proposal to validation and an actual execution receipt. Model agreement is not evidence, and reverting weights does not undo actions.

steps.name: Improve
steps.title: Learn from permitted episodes.
steps.text: Record observations, alternatives, outcomes and reviewed corrections under an explicit collection policy. Derive perception labels, language examples, policy trajectories and world transitions. Train separately, evaluate on held-out tasks and accept a new assignment at a safe boundary.

concept_note: Platform design · integrated roles and model acceptance remain pending
human_text: Define authority. Inspect observed outcomes. Keep stop and revocation on the Rust control path.
faq_intro: What the current foundation does, what the architecture proposes and what still needs evidence.

questions.question: What is Eylema?
questions.answer: Eylema is a platform in development for defining, running and evolving cooperative agentic loops. Stable role contracts connect local participants, Rust execution, decision evidence and permitted training data. The deterministic task console is its first implemented foundation.

questions.question: What works today?
questions.answer: The public core includes typed Rust tasks, deterministic execution, durable recovery, a local loopback service, CLI and browser console. The console creates tasks, runs deterministic actions and inspects persisted state. Verified-human stop authorization remains a separate acceptance requirement. This promotional site does not run the console or establish full-product acceptance.

questions.question: Can I swap models or use XState now?
questions.answer: The architecture proposes compatible model replacement and a local XState workflow adapter. These integrations are not yet accepted runtime features. MiniCPM, Qwen and decision policies require exact supported profiles; arbitrary weights are not interchangeable. Rust remains responsible for authority and execution truth.

questions.question: How are decisions explained?
questions.answer: The proposed evidence record links goals, source observations, alternatives, constraints, model versions, validation and observed outcomes. A readable summary must reference that evidence. Hidden model reasoning is not proof; predictions and suggestions remain distinct from observed facts.

questions.question: Does running a loop permit training on my data?
questions.answer: No. Collection and training need their own purpose, permission, retention and export policy. The proposed dataset builder keeps episode lineage and related samples in the same split, including failures and corrections. Unsloth is an external training tool; no accepted training or model-improvement result is claimed.

questions.question: Which platform comes first?
questions.answer: The first experimental target is a single-user loopback application on a MacBook Pro with Apple M4 Pro and 24 GB unified memory. Browser and native execution have distinct boundaries. Mac mini M4 and Linux RTX equipment are additional inventory, not accepted support; remote access and Linux acceptance are future scope.

questions.question: What is the project license?
questions.answer: Eylema first-party core code and documentation use Apache-2.0. Separately identified third-party material, model weights and datasets retain their own terms. This does not grant a blanket license to every asset or model, or change the website repository license.

foundation_cards.label: Implemented foundation
foundation_cards.title: A local task console.
foundation_cards.text: Owned Rust task contracts, deterministic execution, journal recovery, loopback HTTP, CLI and a browser console. Create and run tasks, inspect progress and reopen persisted state. Verified-person enrollment and stop acceptance remain separate gates.

foundation_cards.label: Architecture v0.5 · proposed integration
foundation_cards.title: A reusable agentic platform.
foundation_cards.text: Versioned loops, role and model registries, inspectable decisions and permitted datasets. MiniCPM perception, Qwen planning, local decision policies and an optional world model are candidates. XState workflow integration requires its own accepted dependency profile.
